title: Automated Discovery of Improved Constant Weight Binary Codes
summary: A constant weight binary code consists of $n$-bit binary codewords, each with exactly $w$ bits equal to 1, such that any two codewords are at least Hamming distance $d$ apart. $A(n,d,w)$ is the maximum size of a constant weight binary code with parameters $n,d,w$. We establish improved lower bounds on $A(n,d,w)$ by constructing new larger codes, for 24 values of $(n,d,w)$ with $6 \leq d \leq 18$ and $18 \leq n \leq 35$.
